how: Calls ask for a concerted effort to build and maintain one shared emblem.
Participants judge the huge logo too demanding for the available support.
A member answers the opening proposal with a bare offer to lend a hand.
The first proposer names an emblem and asks whether others will join.
Starting and recruiting occur in the same proposal rather than as demonstrated successive stages.
A proposer specifies a white emblem on green with a yellow outline.
A participant reads the developing area as a geographic shape and offers it as a design thought.
Builders report individual pixels, outlines, a finished yellow line and border work.
Block references and grids make the image copyable while a marked pixel locates its start.
A progress report answers a concerted call, but recruitment of its author by that call is not independently established.
Posting a block reference does not demonstrate settlement when participants still cannot communicate where the round emblem starts.
The script maker offers unattended maintenance, credits borrowed influence and adjusts colors to preserve neighboring work.
A host moderator attaches a ban warning to recruiting defacement and insists each side build its own work.
A single room with a documented sanction cannot test the stated prevalence of decided order across rooms.
Reports of rival colors and attack prompt calls to preserve the emblem.
The concerted effort anticipates maintenance and a later reply asks for preservation of the attacked work.
The script's stated purpose is unattended upkeep, but the record does not measure a placement-capacity threshold.
Participants distinguish rogue attackers from the treaty's organized parties rather than independently identify every placer.
A truce is attempted, invoked, declared broken and later restated as reciprocal restraint.
An envoy reports carrying a truce proposal to the neighboring subreddit.
Members advocate building their own work and explain the defensive cost of attacking neighbors.
A wall proposal receives agreement constrained by the need to devote resources to defending the emblem.
A reciprocal truce is explicitly invoked as a reason not to vandalize neighboring work.
The appeal to keep a truce also depends on the stated disadvantage in active participants and expected defeat.
Members propose moving a heart to avoid conflict and report contacting another group about space.
Contact about space leaves permission, occupancy and a hosting authority unestablished.
The local relocation account includes switching a developing build because another area is protected by a script, without establishing prior completed-work erasure.
The stated reason for switching is protection by another script, not demonstrably the separately reported shortage of support.
An outside group is asked for help and supplied coordinates, without evidence here that it sends assistance.
Members invite help covering a rival with another group's flag.
Visitors ask the room for help, without demonstrating delivery in the cited turns.
An outside help request is documented, but the arrow's additional claim that helpers arrive remains unestablished.
The agreement leads to an intended mutually protective script, not a documented completed exchange of protective labor.
A neighboring bot writer invites the local script maker into a shared discussion channel.
A request for easier conversation is answered by identifying the lack of a known local channel before offering the neighbor's channel.
Joint maintenance is proposed, but the final combined script is expressly reported as unimplemented.
Defensive cooperation reaches agreement and a prospective shared script, not demonstrated joint defense through that script.
Blaming treaty-ignorant rogues does not establish an explicit dispute over who may bind the room.
A reported treaty problem is answered by rogue attribution without an explicit challenge to representative authority.
The preexisting sports rivalry is invoked while advocating conversion of a rival's emblem.
The conversion call names champions and the rival emblem in the same turn.
Participants preserve ordinary rivalry banter while explicitly suspending vandalism under a canvas truce.
A local player-name joke enters a construction exchange as playful acknowledgment.
Repeated player-name posts and variations enact the host's separately explained April Fools joke.
Alternative names and a mocking variant push against the repeated player-name refrain.
Questions about the refrain and a ban-as-joke complaint expose uncertainty without verifying a ban.
A moderator evaluates the disruptive prank and suggests preserving more host functionality next year.
A separate fake story is praised and graded for the effort to make it look real.
A moderator requests that canvas discussion be contained in one hub.
Members reject the canvas activity or question whether bots defeat its purpose.
Calls precede containment, but the moderator instruction does not establish recruitment volume as its cause.
Ending talk combines regret, thanks for scripting and celebration of lasting representation.
The final-image thread records survival and explains the unrealized protective agreement.
A surviving visible mark warrants celebration even though its organizers say planned additions remained unfinished.
Celebrating and recording occur together in the final-image post, without demonstrating celebration caused recording.
Regret about unfinished canvas work does not document a decision to carry the effort forward.
The recorded final image is not followed by a documented decision about a future canvas or retained organization.
An imperfect final picture and regret do not establish a dispute about cleanup, historical correction or the retained version.
Recurring instructions propose replacing rival lettering with cheers or insults, and one member reports an ongoing attempt.
Posts recruit conversion or replacement of a rival emblem.
Attack proposals occur within a recruitment effort, without demonstrating that recruitment caused participants to attack.
Attack calls receive direct replies explaining host sanctions or retaliation costs as reasons for restraint.
A war call receives an explicit appeal to keep the existing truce because the other side has more active people.
Rivalry is carried through a proposed taunt and celebration of the rival's reported removal.
Closing consolation celebrates the rival's removal alongside regret about unfinished local work.
Attack proposals and victory talk are documented, but no demonstrated successful local raid links them causally.
